extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in Indian news, comedy, and freedom-of-speech developments
extracted.subtask_description: A news-summary article describing the arrest of Indian stand-up comic Munawar Faruqui, the complaint that precipitated it, legal provisions cited, public and peer reactions, and immediate legal outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 295-A (outraging religious feelings)
rubrics_metrics.description: section 295-A which deals with deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article identifies 295-A of the Indian Penal Code as one of the sections under which Faruqui was arrested; allegations that jokes about deities were 'indecent' can be framed as deliberate/malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings, triggering this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrest under 'various sections of the Indian Penal Code'
rubrics_metrics.description: Faruqui was then arrested under various sections of the Indian Penal Code, including section 295-A...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complaint by an attendee (in this case by Eklavya Singh Gaud, son of a BJP MLA) alleging indecent remarks can lead to organizers being forced to stop a show and subsequent police action invoking multiple IPC provisions; the article indicates arrest can follow such complaints even if contested publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for complaint/witnessing indecent jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Gaud had said that he and his associates went to watch the show and they witnessed Faruqui allegedly make indecent jokes about Hindu deities. Gaud further said that he forced the organizers to stop the show soon after that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practical trigger described is attendee testimony alleging 'indecent jokes about Hindu deities' and immediate disruption of the event; such firsthand complaints are presented as the factual basis used to lodge charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and peer reaction to arrests of comedians
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedian Vir Das ... tweeted, 'Asking for a friend. Jokes about God are wrong, got it. But jokes about people who get upset about jokes about God are cool right?' Other comedians also indirectly hit out at the administration for Faruqui’s arrest including Amit Tandon and Kunal Kamra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article presents industry and public reactions as part of the context: peer criticism of the arrest frames debates about acceptable humor, the boundary between jokes and offence, and social support or condemnation, which can influence public discourse and perceived legitimacy of legal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim bail as immediate legal outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: While, Faruqui received interim bail on Friday, many have questioned the very grounds on which he was arrested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim bail is noted as the short-term legal remedy following arrest; the article uses this to indicate the case moved to judicial process and to highlight public questioning of the arrest grounds.
